mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over the last two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and overall economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increasing housing starts (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% over the last two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increasing industrial production (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points and nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 100,000 within the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp and PAYEMS increases > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of improving labor market conditions (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures rise by more than 1% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% over the last two months, it signals inflationary pressures and strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of rising consumption and inflation (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production increases by more than 0.5% and real GDP increases by more than 0.5% over the last quarter, it signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increase > 0.5% and GDPC1 increase > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of increasing industrial production and GDP (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
